messages.content: if i say there is fish on the plate, am i talking about food or a fish as an animal?
it could be about food, but more of the sentence can help make it clear. we are eating fish is about food, while a fish lives in water is about the animal.
use eating and water in a simple answer.
we are eating fish is about food. a fish lives in water is about the animal. the word can have a different meaning with different words around it.
keep it simple.
we are eating fish is about food. a fish lives in water is about an animal. the words around fish help make clear what you mean.
now i want a story about a child looking at a fish, not eating it.
a child sat near a container of water and watched a fish move. she put her book down and watched it for a while. then she drew the fish on a page, with the water around it.
say that part simply.
she put her book down and watched the fish for a while.
does the word fish by itself tell you a person ate it?
no. you need the rest of the sentence or conversation to know whether it is about food, an animal, or another use of the word.
write one short question to check which meaning i want.
do you mean fish as food or a fish as an animal?
i tried to sing a song with my sister today. i do not sing well, but i liked hearing us together.
you can enjoy that time without making it a test of who can sing best. what part did you like most?
i liked that she waited when i lost the words. she did not start the whole song again, just gave me time to come back in.
then you had someone making room for you to keep trying. the song could go on without every small stop being the whole problem.
keep it simple.
you tried to sing with your sister and liked being together. when you lost the words, she gave you time so you could keep trying.
use sing in a sentence about what i like.
you like to sing with your sister because she gives you time when you lose the words.
write a short thank you to her. keep it simple.
thank you for waiting when i forgot the words. i liked trying the song together.
use the song in a simple thank you.
thank you for giving me time when i forgot the words. i liked trying the song together.
keep the thank you simple.
thank you for giving me time when i forgot the words. i liked trying the song together.
write a story about a person who is late for a vehicle they wanted to take to visit a friend. they should ask about another way instead of saying the whole visit is lost.

a woman came to the station just after the vehicle she wanted had left. she stood near the door for a moment, then asked a worker what she could do next. the worker showed her where to find the next time. before choosing, she called her friend to say the journey would be later than she first thought. her friend said the afternoon was still free. she sat down to wait, now knowing what to check before she went.
make the story simple.
a woman got to the station after the vehicle she wanted had left. she asked about the next one and called her friend. the friend said a later visit was still okay, so she waited for the new journey.
why ask the friend instead of only finding another vehicle?
because the time of the visit changes too. another journey might work for her, but her friend still needs to know and say whether the later time is good.
write the call as a short conversation.
i did not get the first vehicle. would it still be okay if i came later? yes, i am free this afternoon. thank you, i will check the next time and tell you when i can get there.
what is still not known at the end of that call?
the time she will get there is still open. she has said she will check, not that she already has the answer.
answer simply.
she still needs to find out when she can get there. her friend knows it will be later, but not the hour yet.
i want to ask if my brother read a book yesterday. is did you reading the book right?
use: did you read the book yesterday? after did in this question, read is the word you want, not reading.
can you make it about my sister instead of asking my brother?
did my sister read the book yesterday?
ask my last request simply.
make it a question about my sister, not a question i say to my brother.
now i want to ask whether she was in the middle of reading when i called.
was my sister reading the book when i called?
what is different about that question?
it asks whether the reading was happening at the time of the call. did she read the book yesterday asks about reading on that day, without choosing that one moment.
give a simple difference.
one asks about yesterday. the other asks about what was happening when you called.
now write a short answer saying she was reading when i called, but i do not know if she finished.
she was reading when you called. you have not told me whether she finished the book.
i say the cup is on the right of the table. my sister looks from the other side and says it is on the left. can both words be about the same cup?
yes. left and right can change with where a person is looking from. the cup can stay in one place. a person on one side can call it right, and a person on the opposite side can call it left.
say it simply.
you can look from one side and call it right. your sister can look from the opposite side and call it left. the cup itself does not have to move.
what can we say if we need one clear place for a story?
you can say whose way of looking you mean, or use another detail like near the window or near the door. that keeps the place clear without changing with every person.
make the idea about the window simple.
you can say the cup is near the window. then both people can look for the same detail.
now i say the cup is near the window, and my sister sees it there too. did we move it by changing our words?
no. you only chose a way to talk about its place that both of you could use. the cup stayed near the window in the example.
can i still use right if i say from my place at the table?
yes. from my place at the table, the cup is on the right makes clear whose way of looking you mean.
write that as one simple sentence.
from my place at the table, the cup is on the right, near the window.
in a made up plan, i want to visit my aunt at two and my cousin at two too. they live far apart, and i can only be at one house at a time. what needs changing?
you need a different time for one visit, or choose only one for that hour. being at one house at two does not let you be at the other far away house at the same moment.
use time in a simple answer.
you need a different time for one visit, or only one visit at two.
now my aunt says three is good. my cousin can still meet at two. do we know the whole plan works?
not yet. you still need to know how long the visit with your cousin and the journey to your aunt will take. changing the hour helps, but it does not by itself give enough time.
ask my last question simply.
if my cousin can meet at two and my aunt at three, do we know the whole plan will work?
now i say i need an hour with my cousin and another hour for the journey.
then going to your cousin at two would use the time until three, and the journey would take you to four. in that example, you cannot get to your aunt at three without changing something.
write a short question asking my aunt about four.
would four work for my visit instead of three?
she says yes. give the whole order.
you visit your cousin at two for an hour, then spend another hour on the journey and get to your aunt at four.

make this shorter but keep the reason and request: i cannot meet in the morning because i have work that i need to finish, and i would like to ask if it would be possible for us to meet after lunch instead.
i need to finish work in the morning. could we meet after lunch instead?
now make it one sentence and keep the reason.
i need to finish work in the morning, so could we meet after lunch instead?
ask my last request simply.
make it one sentence and keep the reason.
can you make it kind without adding a big story?
i would like to see you, but i need to finish work in the morning. could we meet after lunch instead?
say my request simply.
make it kind and simple without adding a long story.
now keep the two sentences and only change lunch to dinner.
i would like to see you, but i need to finish work in the morning. could we meet after dinner instead?
does changing lunch to dinner mean the morning work takes all day?
no. it changes the time you ask to meet. the message still only says the work is in the morning, not that it goes on until dinner.
answer simply.
no. you changed the meeting time. you did not say how long the work takes after the morning.
picoboi, help me choose a story idea. ask one question before giving me an idea.
would you like the story to happen at home or outside?
ask it simply.
would you like the story to happen at home or outside?
at home. make it about someone finding an old letter, but leave who sent it open.

a person is cleaning a shelf at home and finds an old letter between two books. the paper has a few words on the front, but the person does not open it right away. the story can stay with the choice of reading it now or asking someone else about it first.
ask my last request simply.
make it about someone finding an old letter at home, but leave who sent it open.
now i choose that the person asks their mother about it first. what can happen next without saying who sent it?
the mother could look at the writing and say she can remember the day the letter came, but not tell the whole story yet. then the person has a question to ask before opening it.
make that simple.
the mother can remember the day the letter came, but the story does not yet say who wrote it.
use can remember in a simple answer.
the mother can remember the day the letter came, but the story does not yet say who wrote it.
